Mailbox is free software: GPL-3.0-only, copyright wander wildwood for what is written here. It is built on Thunderbird for Android; that and everything else it bundles keeps its own license, listed below.
Any mail account that takes a password, read and written in black and white, a page at a time. Thunderbird for Android, redrawn for this screen.

It connects only to the mail servers you enter. Nothing is sent to us, and your address and password stay on this phone. Setting up an account, it also asks the address\'s own domain, DNS, which may be Google Public DNS, and Mozilla\'s list of mail providers, the last two told the domain and not the address. \"Feed the llamas\" in About opens a donation page (square.link) in your browser, only when you press it. The app sends nothing there; if you give, the payment is handled on that page by Square, not by this app.

After Thunderbird for Android, by MZLA Technologies and the K-9 Mail contributors, Apache 2.0. Lato by Łukasz Dziedzic, SIL Open Font License 1.1. The libraries it bundles are each under their own license.

This app is provided as it is, without any warranty of any kind, as the GNU General Public License says, and you use it at your own risk. It is not made or endorsed by Mozilla, MZLA Technologies or the Thunderbird project. A donation through \"Feed the llamas\" is voluntary and unlocks nothing: the app is the same with or without one.

This app is made by wander wildwood, an independent developer: one person, not a company. That makes wander wildwood the data controller for anything the app itself handles, and that is very little. What you put in stays on this phone. The only things that go out are the requests described above: the connections to your mail servers, which carry your login and the mail you fetch and send; when you set up an account, a lookup that tells the address\'s own domain, DNS (possibly Google Public DNS) and Mozilla\'s list of mail providers the domain, not the address; and the pictures in a message, fetched from wherever the sender put them when you choose to show them. Nothing comes to the developer.
Write to email@wanderthe.dev, about your data or anything else.

Under the GDPR you can ask to see the data held about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to limit or object to its use, to take a copy with you, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a data protection authority. Since the app keeps what it stores only on your phone, you can do most of this yourself: remove an account or delete mail in the app, export your settings to a file, clear the app\'s data in Android\'s settings, or uninstall the app. What your mail provider, Mozilla\'s autoconfig service and Google Public DNS receive is covered by their own privacy policies.
